newsitem.title: FRANCE: Iraq's Tareq Aziz to visit France.
newsitem.headline: Iraq's Tareq Aziz to visit France.

text.p: Iraqi Deputy Prime Minister Tareq Aziz will visit Paris next week for talks with French leaders, reflecting cautiously improving ties with Baghdad, a French official said on Thursday.

Confirming a report in the international Arabic-language daily a-Hayat, the official said Aziz would meet French Prime Minister Alain Juppe and Foreign Minister Herve de Charette but would not be received by President Jacques Chirac.
Aziz, who last visited France in December 1995, is due to arrive in Paris on January 14.

His visit comes after the French government, distancing itself from the United States, last month pulled out of western air patrols over Kurdish regions of northern Iraq, saying the operation was no longer part of a humanitarian relief effort.

France remains part of the coalition with the United States and Britain that patrols the skies over southern Iraq to protect Kuwait and Saudi Arabia, but it pointedly refused to endorse U.S. air raids on Iraq last year in retaliation for the Iraqi army's intervention in intra-Kurdish fighting.
The French campaigned hard in favour of a U.N. oil-for-food exchange allowing Baghdad to feed undernourished civilians, hit by U.N. economic sanctions since before the 1991 Gulf War.

Two French oil companies, Total and Elf-Aquitaine are among the firms buying Iraqi oil under the programme and have signed long-term deals to help renew its oil industry once an oil sales embargo is eased.
Iraq was long a prime client for French arms and capital goods and owes Paris about $5 billion.
